title: Inventory Synchronization for Regional Retailers
business: A regional retail chain managing inventory across multiple physical storefronts and a centralized e-commerce platform.
problem: The retailer faces data inconsistency where local store inventory updates are not reflected in the central database in real-time, leading to overselling of items during high-traffic periods.
solution: Implementing MariaDB Galera Cluster provides synchronous multi-master replication, ensuring that every node in the cluster contains the same data set at all times, allowing any node to handle read and write operations reliably.
steps: Configure individual MariaDB Server instances on separate network nodes.
Install and enable the wsrep provider plugin to manage cluster state synchronization.
Define the cluster address and node address in the configuration files to establish peer discovery.
Initialize the cluster on the primary node and join subsequent nodes to the existing cluster.
Verify cluster status using the wsrep_local_state_comment variable to ensure all nodes are in sync.
outcome: The retailer achieves high availability and strong consistency across all locations, preventing inventory discrepancies and improving the customer checkout experience.
limitation: A significant tradeoff is the write latency overhead caused by the synchronous replication protocol, which requires all nodes to agree on a transaction before it is committed; this can be checked by monitoring the wsrep_flow_control_paused status variable.

questions.question: In Inventory Synchronization for Regional Retailers, what is the primary reason for adopting MariaDB Galera Cluster?
options: To enable synchronous multi-master replication for data consistency
To reduce the total number of database servers required
To provide a read-only archive for historical inventory data
To automatically migrate data from MySQL to MariaDB
questions.explanation: The scenario identifies data inconsistency as the core problem, which Galera Cluster solves through synchronous replication.

options: Increased risk of data loss during power outages
Write latency overhead due to synchronous transaction commitment
Inability to perform read operations on secondary nodes
questions.explanation: Synchronous replication requires coordination across nodes, which introduces latency during the commit phase.
questions.evidence: A significant tradeoff is the write latency overhead caused by the synchronous replication protocol, which requires all nodes to agree on a transaction before it is committed
